subproblems.title: Cone-type inequality: a finite-mass cycle in a small ball acts weakly on a fixed test form
subproblems.statement: Assume (VO), the exact frozen statement of dtc_vanish_off_support, which appears verbatim as the first hypothesis of the Lean statement: for all P, n ∈ ℕ, every U ⊆ ℝ^P, every current S ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U n) and every test form ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) (TestFormOn U n) whose topological support is disjoint from spt S, S(ω) = 0. Then for all P, n ∈ ℕ and every test form ω ∈ 𝒟^{n+1}(ℝ^P) there is a real number c ≥ 0 such that for every current X ∈ 𝒟_{n+1}(ℝ^P) with ∂X = 0 and M(X) < ∞, every x₀ ∈ ℝ^P and every ϱ > 0 with spt X ⊆ B̄_ϱ(x₀) (closed ball), |X(ω)| ≤ c·ϱ·M(X). Here M(X) = X.mass = M_{ℝ^P}(X) (Simon 6.2.4–6.2.5, Euclidean coefficient norm), read as a real number (ENNReal.toReal).
subproblems.lean_statement: (∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (S : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (ω : TestFormOn U n), Disjoint (tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n)) S.support → S ω = 0) → ∀ (P n : ℕ) (ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (n + 1)), ∃ c : ℝ, 0 ≤ c ∧ ∀ (X : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (n + 1)) (x₀ : Euclid P) (ϱ : ℝ), 0 < ϱ → X.boundary = 0 → X.mass < ∞ → X.support ⊆ closedBall x₀ ϱ → |X ω| ≤ c * ϱ * X.mass.toReal
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Step 0 of the supplied proof (cone inequality, parent T3; Simon Ch. 6, 2.27/2.30 as used in 8.2(4)–(6)), specialized to the form in which the parent uses it: for a fixed test form ω the constant may depend on ω, so the homotopy-operator bound ϱ·M(X)·‖dω‖_∞ is replaced by ϱ·M(X)·c_ω with c_ω a Lipschitz constant of ω; the homotopy formula is then only needed for constant forms, where it is the identity d((n+1)⁻¹ ι_{x−x₀} α) = α.

Notation. For a k-covector β on ℝ^P (a continuous alternating k-linear map) |β| := covectorEuclideanNorm β = (Σ_I β(e_{I(1)}, …, e_{I(k)})²)^{1/2}, the sum over strictly increasing I : {1,…,k} → {1,…,P}, e_1, …, e_P the standard basis; ‖β‖ is the operator norm. Test forms are smooth compactly supported forms (TestFormOn univ). For Y ∈ 𝒟_{n+1}(ℝ^P), M(Y) = M_{ℝ^P}(Y) = sup{max(Y(φ), 0) : φ ∈ 𝒟^{n+1}(ℝ^P), |φ(x)| ≤ 1 for all x} (GeometricCurrentOn.massOn univ, the supremum taken in [0, ∞]); spt Y is ℝ^P minus the union of all open sets with compact closure on which Y vanishes.

1. (Homogeneity.) For t ∈ ℝ, |tβ| = |t|·|β|: every coefficient of tβ is t times the corresponding coefficient of β, so |tβ|² = Σ_I t²β(e_I)² = t²|β|² and |tβ| = √(t²)·|β| = |t|·|β|. (SimonGMT only provides covectorEuclideanNorm_neg and covectorEuclideanNorm_nonneg, so this is proved as a local lemma by unfolding covectorEuclideanNorm and using Finset.mul_sum, Real.sqrt_mul and Real.sqrt_sq_eq_abs.) In particular |−β| = |β|, and |β| ≥ 0.

2. (Coefficient norm versus operator norm.) |β| ≤ P^{k/2}·‖β‖: each coefficient satisfies |β(e_{I(1)}, …, e_{I(k)})| ≤ ‖β‖·Π_i ‖e_{I(i)}‖ = ‖β‖ (ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm), and there are at most P^k index maps I, so |β|² ≤ P^k‖β‖².

3. (Mass controls evaluations.) Let Y ∈ 𝒟_{n+1}(ℝ^P) with M(Y) < ∞, φ ∈ 𝒟^{n+1}(ℝ^P) and s ≥ 0 with |φ(x)| ≤ s for all x. Then |Y(φ)| ≤ s·M(Y). Indeed, let t > s (so t > 0). The test forms t⁻¹φ and −t⁻¹φ have topological support in ℝ^P and, by step 1, |±t⁻¹φ(x)| = t⁻¹|φ(x)| ≤ s/t ≤ 1 for all x, so both are admissible in the supremum defining M(Y). Since Y is linear, ±t⁻¹·Y(φ) = Y(±t⁻¹φ) ≤ M(Y) (GeometricCurrentOn.le_massOn, M(Y) finite). Hence |Y(φ)| ≤ t·M(Y) for every t > s, and therefore |Y(φ)| ≤ s·M(Y).

4. (The constant c.) ω is C^∞ with compact support, so its derivative Dω : ℝ^P → L(ℝ^P, Λ^{n+1}(ℝ^P)) is continuous with compact support (HasCompactSupport.fderiv), hence bounded: ‖Dω(x)‖ ≤ L₀ for all x, for some L₀ ≥ 0. By the mean value inequality on the convex set ℝ^P, ‖ω(x) − ω(y)‖ ≤ L₀|x − y| for all x, y. Put c := P^{(n+1)/2}·L₀ ≥ 0. By step 2, |ω(x) − ω(y)| ≤ c|x − y| for all x, y ∈ ℝ^P. The number c depends only on ω (and P, n), not on X, x₀ or ϱ.

5. (Cut-off.) Fix X, x₀ and ϱ > 0 as in the statement, and ε > 0. Let ζ : ℝ^P → [0, 1] be the smooth bump function centred at x₀ with inner radius ϱ + ε/2 and outer radius ϱ + ε (Mathlib ContDiffBump): ζ = 1 on B̄_{ϱ+ε/2}(x₀), ζ(x) = 0 whenever |x − x₀| ≥ ϱ + ε, and ζ has compact support. Put G := B_{ϱ+ε/2}(x₀), an open set with spt X ⊆ B̄_ϱ(x₀) ⊆ G and ζ = 1 on G.

6. (Localization.) For every φ ∈ 𝒟^{n+1}(ℝ^P), X(φ) = X(ζφ). Indeed (1 − ζ)φ is smooth and its support lies in the compact set tsupport φ, so it is a test form; it vanishes on the open set G, hence its topological support is contained in the closed set ℝ^P ∖ G, which is disjoint from spt X. By (VO) (with U = ℝ^P, S = X), X((1 − ζ)φ) = 0, and by linearity X(φ) = X(ζφ) + X((1 − ζ)φ) = X(ζφ).

7. (Constant forms are boundaries near spt X.) Let α := ω(x₀) ∈ Λ^{n+1}(ℝ^P) and define the n-form ψ(x) := (n + 1)⁻¹·α.curryLeft(x − x₀), i.e. ψ(x)(v₁, …, v_n) = (n + 1)⁻¹·α(x − x₀, v₁, …, v_n). ψ is affine in x, hence smooth, and it has derivative Dψ(x) = (n + 1)⁻¹·α.curryLeft at every x (chain rule for the continuous linear map α.curryLeft composed with y ↦ y − x₀, then HasFDerivAt.const_smul). The exterior derivative is extDeriv ψ(x) = alternatizeUncurryFin(Dψ(x)) (definition of Mathlib's extDeriv, which is SimonGMT's exteriorDerivative), so dψ(x) = alternatizeUncurryFin((n + 1)⁻¹·α.curryLeft) = (n + 1)⁻¹·alternatizeUncurryFin(α.curryLeft) (ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFin_smul) = (n + 1)⁻¹·((n + 1) • α) (ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFin_curryLeft, where (n + 1) • α is a natural-number multiple, rewritten as the real multiple ((n + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ)·α by Nat.cast_smul_eq_nsmul) = α for every x. The n-form ζψ is smooth with compact support, so it is a test form, and d(ζψ) is a test form. On the open set G we have ζψ = ψ, so for x ∈ G the germs agree and d(ζψ)(x) = dψ(x) = α = ζ(x)α (Filter.EventuallyEq.extDeriv_eq). Hence the test form ζα − d(ζψ) (ζα is smooth with compact support) vanishes on G, its topological support lies in ℝ^P ∖ G and is disjoint from spt X, and (VO) gives X(ζα − d(ζψ)) = 0. Since ∂X = 0, X(d(ζψ)) = ∂X(ζψ) = 0. Therefore X(ζα) = 0.

8. (Estimate.) By steps 6 and 7, X(ω) = X(ζω) − X(ζα) = X(φ), where φ := ζ(ω − α) = ζω − ζα ∈ 𝒟^{n+1}(ℝ^P). For every x ∈ ℝ^P either ζ(x) = 0, so φ(x) = 0, or |x − x₀| < ϱ + ε and then, by steps 1 and 4, |φ(x)| = ζ(x)·|ω(x) − ω(x₀)| ≤ c|x − x₀| ≤ c(ϱ + ε). By step 3 (with Y := X and s := c(ϱ + ε)), |X(ω)| ≤ c(ϱ + ε)·M(X).

9. Since ε > 0 was arbitrary, |X(ω)| ≤ c·ϱ·M(X). ∎
proof_key_steps: Mass controls evaluations: |Y(φ)| ≤ (sup_x |φ(x)|)·M(Y) by rescaling ±φ into the admissible class of M(Y).
Lipschitz constant c of ω in the Euclidean coefficient norm from the bounded derivative of ω and |β| ≤ P^{k/2}‖β‖.
Cut-off ζ ≡ 1 on B_{ϱ+ε/2}(x₀) with support in B_{ϱ+ε}(x₀); (VO) gives X(φ) = X(ζφ).
The constant form α = ω(x₀) equals dψ for ψ = (n+1)⁻¹ ι_{x−x₀} α (alternatizeUncurryFin_curryLeft); (VO) and ∂X = 0 give X(ζα) = 0.
X(ω) = X(ζ(ω − α)) with |ζ(ω − α)| ≤ c(ϱ + ε), so |X(ω)| ≤ c(ϱ + ε)M(X); let ε ↓ 0.

subproblems.title: Besicovitch–Vitali covering inequality for set integrals of a bounded density
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, μ a Borel measure on ℝ^P with μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K, g : ℝ^P → ℝ μ-a.e. strongly measurable with |g(x)| ≤ 1 for μ-a.e. x, θ ∈ ℝ with θ ≤ 1, W ⊆ ℝ^P open with μ(W) < ∞, and E ⊆ W an arbitrary (not necessarily measurable) set. Assume that for every x ∈ E and every δ > 0 there is ρ ∈ (0, δ) with ∫_{B̄_ρ(x)} g dμ ≤ θ·μ(B̄_ρ(x)) (closed ball; μ(B̄_ρ(x)) read as a real number). Then ∫_W g dμ ≤ μ(W) − (1 − θ)·μ(E), where μ(E) ≤ μ(W) < ∞ is the (outer) measure of E and all measures are read as real numbers (ENNReal.toReal).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (g : Euclid P → ℝ) (θ : ℝ) (E W : Set (Euclid P)), (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → μ K < ∞) → AEStronglyMeasurable g μ → (∀ᵐ x ∂μ, |g x| ≤ 1) → θ ≤ 1 → IsOpen W → E ⊆ W → μ W < ∞ → (∀ x ∈ E, ∀ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ → ∃ ρ : ℝ, 0 < ρ ∧ ρ < δ ∧ ∫ y in closedBall x ρ, g y ∂μ ≤ θ * (μ (closedBall x ρ)).toReal) → ∫ y in W, g y ∂μ ≤ (μ W).toReal - (1 - θ) * (μ E).toReal
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the covering part of Step 7 and the measure bookkeeping of Step 9 of the supplied proof (Simon Ch. 6, 8.2: pairwise disjoint closed balls covering μ-almost all of the low-density set, with Σμ(B_i) ≤ μ(W)), stated for a fixed bounded density g (in the parent g = ξ(ω) for a fixed test form ω).

1. (σ-finiteness and integrability.) ℝ^P = ⋃_k B̄_k(0) and every closed ball is compact, so μ(B̄_k(0)) < ∞; hence μ is σ-finite, in particular s-finite. (In Lean, register IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts μ from the hypothesis ∀ K compact, μ K < ∞; the instances IsLocallyFiniteMeasure, SigmaFinite and SFinite on Euclid P then follow, as required by Besicovitch.exists_disjoint_closedBall_covering_ae.) Since g is μ-a.e. strongly measurable and |g| ≤ 1 μ-a.e., g is integrable on every measurable set of finite μ-measure, in particular on W and on every closed ball.

2. (Admissible radii.) For x ∈ ℝ^P let f(x) := {ρ > 0 : B̄_ρ(x) ⊆ W and ∫_{B̄_ρ(x)} g dμ ≤ θ·μ(B̄_ρ(x))}. For every x ∈ E and δ > 0, f(x) ∩ (0, δ) ≠ ∅: since W is open and x ∈ E ⊆ W, there is r > 0 with B_r(x) ⊆ W; the hypothesis applied with min(δ, r) gives ρ ∈ (0, min(δ, r)) with the integral inequality, and B̄_ρ(x) ⊆ B_r(x) ⊆ W.

3. (Besicovitch covering.) ℝ^P is a finite-dimensional real normed space, hence second countable with the Besicovitch covering property, and μ is an s-finite Borel measure. By Mathlib Besicovitch.exists_disjoint_closedBall_covering_ae (applied to μ, f, the set E and R ≡ 1) there are a countable set t ⊆ E and r : ℝ^P → ℝ such that r(x) ∈ f(x) for every x ∈ t, the closed balls B_x := B̄_{r(x)}(x), x ∈ t, are pairwise disjoint, and μ(E ∖ V) = 0 for V := ⋃_{x∈t} B_x.

4. V is measurable (a countable union of closed sets) and V ⊆ W (each B_x ⊆ W because r(x) ∈ f(x)), so μ(V) ≤ μ(W) < ∞. Since E ⊆ V ∪ (E ∖ V), μ(E) ≤ μ(V) + μ(E ∖ V) = μ(V).

5. (Integral over V.) By countable additivity of μ and of the integral over the countable family of pairwise disjoint measurable sets B_x, x ∈ t (Mathlib measure_iUnion and MeasureTheory.integral_iUnion, using that g is integrable on V ⊆ W), μ(V) = Σ_{x∈t} μ(B_x), a convergent series of finite reals, and ∫_V g dμ = Σ_{x∈t} ∫_{B_x} g dμ, a series that converges absolutely because |∫_{B_x} g dμ| ≤ μ(B_x). Since r(x) ∈ f(x), every term satisfies ∫_{B_x} g dμ ≤ θ·μ(B_x); summing, ∫_V g dμ ≤ θ·Σ_{x∈t} μ(B_x) = θ·μ(V).

6. (Integral over W ∖ V.) Since g ≤ 1 μ-a.e., ∫_{W∖V} g dμ ≤ μ(W ∖ V) = μ(W) − μ(V) (finite measures, V ⊆ W).

7. (Conclusion.) ∫_W g dμ = ∫_{W∖V} g dμ + ∫_V g dμ ≤ μ(W) − μ(V) + θ·μ(V) = μ(W) − (1 − θ)·μ(V) ≤ μ(W) − (1 − θ)·μ(E), using 1 − θ ≥ 0 and μ(E) ≤ μ(V) from step 4 (all quantities are finite reals). ∎
proof_key_steps: μ is σ-finite and g is integrable on sets of finite measure.
Admissible radii f(x): closed balls inside W satisfying the integral inequality, available at arbitrarily small scales at every x ∈ E.
Besicovitch (exists_disjoint_closedBall_covering_ae): countable disjoint admissible balls B_x with μ(E ∖ ⋃B_x) = 0.
Countable additivity: ∫_V g ≤ θμ(V); and ∫_{W∖V} g ≤ μ(W) − μ(V).
Combine with μ(E) ≤ μ(V) and θ ≤ 1.

subproblems.title: Good slicing radii below a low-density scale
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ with n ≥ 1, μ a Borel measure on ℝ^P with μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K, x₁ ∈ ℝ^P, a > 0 and s > 0 with μ(B_s(x₁)) < (a·s)^n (open ball), and N ⊆ ℝ a Lebesgue-null set. Then there is ρ with 0 < ρ < s and ρ ∉ N such that μ(∂B_ρ(x₁)) = 0 (∂B_ρ(x₁) = sphere x₁ ρ) and liminf_{h→0, h>0} h⁻¹·μ({x : ρ − h < |x − x₁| < ρ}) ≤ 2na·F^{(n−1)/n}, where F = μ(B_ρ(x₁)) read as a real number (real power), the liminf is taken in [0, ∞] along 𝓝[>] 0 with ENNReal.ofReal h⁻¹, and the right side is ENNReal.ofReal of the real number 2na·F^{(n−1)/n}.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (x₁ : Euclid P) (a s : ℝ) (N : Set ℝ), (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → μ K < ∞) → 1 ≤ n → 0 < a → 0 < s → μ (ball x₁ s) < ENNReal.ofReal ((a * s) ^ n) → volume N = 0 → ∃ ρ : ℝ, 0 < ρ ∧ ρ < s ∧ ρ ∉ N ∧ μ (sphere x₁ ρ) = 0 ∧ liminf (fun h : ℝ => ENNReal.ofReal h⁻¹ * μ {x | ρ - h < dist x x₁ ∧ dist x x₁ < ρ}) (𝓝[>] 0) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (2 * n * a * (μ (ball x₁ ρ)).toReal ^ (((n : ℝ) - 1) / n))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Steps 3 and 5 of the supplied proof (Simon Ch. 6, 8.2 (2)–(3): radii where (F^{1/n})' is controlled, and F' = nF^{(n−1)/n}(F^{1/n})').

1. For r ∈ ℝ let F(r) := μ(B_r(x₁)), a finite real number (B_r(x₁) ⊆ B̄_r(x₁), which is compact). F is nondecreasing and F(r) = 0 for r ≤ 0 (the ball is empty). Let G(r) := F(r)^{1/n} (real power of a nonnegative number); G is nondecreasing, G(r) = 0 for r ≤ 0, and G(r)^n = F(r) for every r (Real.rpow_inv_natCast_pow, n ≥ 1).

2. From μ(B_s(x₁)) < (as)^n we get F(s) < (as)^n and hence G(s) < as, because u ↦ u^{1/n} is strictly increasing on [0, ∞) and as > 0.

3. Let G' := deriv G (equal to 0 where G is not differentiable); G' ≥ 0 everywhere (Monotone.deriv_nonneg). Since G is monotone on [0, s], Mathlib MonotoneOn.intervalIntegrable_deriv and MonotoneOn.intervalIntegral_deriv_mem_uIcc show that G' is integrable on [0, s] and ∫_0^s G' ≤ G(s) − G(0) = G(s) < as.

4. Let E := {r ∈ (0, s) : G'(r) ≤ 2a}; it is measurable (deriv G is measurable, measurable_deriv). E has positive Lebesgue measure: otherwise G'(r) > 2a for a.e. r ∈ (0, s), and then ∫_0^s G' ≥ ∫_0^s 2a = 2as > as, contradicting step 3.

5. The following sets are Lebesgue-null: N (by hypothesis); D := {r : G is not differentiable at r} (Lebesgue's theorem for monotone functions, Mathlib Monotone.ae_differentiableAt); and Q := {r : μ(∂B_r(x₁)) > 0}, which is countable because the spheres ∂B_r(x₁), r ∈ ℝ, are pairwise disjoint closed (measurable) sets and μ is σ-finite (ℝ^P is a countable union of compact balls of finite μ-measure; Mathlib Measure.countable_meas_pos_of_disjoint_iUnion, whose SFinite instance is obtained by registering IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts μ from the hypothesis). Since E has positive measure, E ⊄ N ∪ D ∪ Q; choose ρ ∈ E ∖ (N ∪ D ∪ Q). Then 0 < ρ < s, ρ ∉ N, μ(∂B_ρ(x₁)) = 0, G is differentiable at ρ and G'(ρ) ≤ 2a.

6. Since F = G^n, F is differentiable at ρ with F'(ρ) = n·G(ρ)^{n−1}·G'(ρ) ≤ 2na·G(ρ)^{n−1} = 2na·F(ρ)^{(n−1)/n}, because G(ρ) ≥ 0 and G(ρ)^{n−1} = (F(ρ)^{1/n})^{n−1} = F(ρ)^{(n−1)/n}.

7. For 0 < h < ρ every x with ρ − h < |x − x₁| < ρ lies in B_ρ(x₁) ∖ B_{ρ−h}(x₁), so, the measures being finite and B_{ρ−h}(x₁) ⊆ B_ρ(x₁), μ({ρ − h < |x − x₁| < ρ}) ≤ F(ρ) − F(ρ − h) and h⁻¹·μ({ρ − h < |x − x₁| < ρ}) ≤ h⁻¹(F(ρ) − F(ρ − h)). As h ↓ 0, h⁻¹(F(ρ) − F(ρ − h)) = (F(ρ + (−h)) − F(ρ))/(−h) → F'(ρ), by differentiability of F at ρ (hasDerivAt_iff_tendsto_slope_zero restricted to negative increments). Passing to [0, ∞] with ENNReal.ofReal (continuous and monotone), the liminf along h ↓ 0 of the left side is at most the limit of the right side: liminf_{h↓0} h⁻¹·μ({ρ − h < |x − x₁| < ρ}) ≤ F'(ρ) ≤ 2na·F(ρ)^{(n−1)/n} by step 6. ∎
proof_key_steps: F(r) = μ(B_r(x₁)) and G = F^{1/n} are nondecreasing, vanish for r ≤ 0, and G(s) < as.
∫_0^s G' ≤ G(s) < as (MonotoneOn.intervalIntegral_deriv_mem_uIcc) forces {r ∈ (0,s) : G'(r) ≤ 2a} to have positive measure.
Remove the null sets N, the non-differentiability points of G, and the countable set of radii with μ(∂B_r(x₁)) > 0.
At the chosen ρ, F' = nG^{n−1}G' ≤ 2naF^{(n−1)/n}.
h⁻¹μ{ρ−h < |x−x₁| < ρ} ≤ h⁻¹(F(ρ) − F(ρ−h)) → F'(ρ), so the liminf is ≤ 2naF(ρ)^{(n−1)/n}.

subproblems.title: Mass gap: integer multiplicity 0-currents of mass < 1 vanish
subproblems.statement: Assume (MR), the exact frozen statement of cmc_massOn_eq_imRep_measure, which appears verbatim as the hypothesis of the Lean statement: for all P, n ∈ ℕ, every open U ⊆ ℝ^P, every T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) and every integer multiplicity representation R : IMRep U n of T (R.Represents T), T.massOn W = R.measure W for every open W, where R.measure = (μHE[n] restricted to R.carrier) with density R.mult. Then for every P ∈ ℕ, every integer multiplicity current Z ∈ 𝒟_0(ℝ^P) with M(Z) = Z.mass < 1 is the zero current.

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Step 6 of the supplied proof, case n = 1 (Simon Ch. 6, footnote 5 to 8.2: in dimension n = 1 the slice ∂(T⌞B_r) of small mass vanishes).

1. Since Z is integer multiplicity there is R : IMRep ℝ^P 0 with R.Represents Z, i.e. Z(ω) = R.action(ω) = ∫_{R.carrier} R.mult(x)·R.orient(x)(ω(x)) dμHE[0](x) for every test form ω. By (MR) applied with U = W = ℝ^P (both open), M(Z) = Z.massOn ℝ^P = R.measure(ℝ^P), where R.measure = (μHE[0] restricted to R.carrier) with density R.mult.

2. Suppose x ∈ R.carrier. The singleton {x} is measurable, so R.measure({x}) = ∫_{{x}} R.mult d(μHE[0]⌞R.carrier) = R.mult(x)·μHE[0]({x} ∩ R.carrier) = R.mult(x)·μHE[0]({x}) (withDensity_apply, lintegral_singleton, Measure.restrict_apply). By Mathlib euclideanHausdorffMeasure_zero, μHE[0] = μH[0], and μH[0]({x}) = 1 (hausdorffMeasure_zero_singleton). Since R.mult(x) is a positive natural number (R.mult_pos), R.measure({x}) ≥ 1, hence M(Z) = R.measure(ℝ^P) ≥ R.measure({x}) ≥ 1, contradicting M(Z) < 1.

3. Therefore R.carrier = ∅, and for every test form ω, Z(ω) = R.action(ω) is an integral over the empty set (with respect to μHE[0] restricted to ∅, the zero measure), hence 0. By extensionality of currents (GeometricCurrentOn.ext), Z = 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: Take an IMRep R of Z; by (MR) with U = W = ℝ^P, M(Z) = R.measure(ℝ^P).
If x ∈ R.carrier then R.measure({x}) = R.mult(x)·μHE[0]({x}) = R.mult(x) ≥ 1 (μHE[0] = μH[0], μH[0]{x} = 1).
M(Z) < 1 forces R.carrier = ∅, so every value Z(ω) is an integral over ∅ and Z = 0.

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Step 4 of the supplied proof (Simon Ch. 6, 8.2 (1)–(2) and 4.9: for a cycle, ∂(T⌞B_r(x₁)) is integer multiplicity for a.e. r and its mass is bounded by the derivative of r ↦ μ(B_r(x₁))).

1. Let f(x) := dist(x, x₁) = |x − x₁|. f is 1-Lipschitz (LipschitzWith.dist_left), {x : f(x) < t} = B_t(x₁) and {x : t − h < f(x) < t} = {x : t − h < |x − x₁| < t}. Let μ' := 0 (the zero measure) and ξ' := 0 (the zero field of d-vectors). Then (μ', ξ') is an admissible representation of ∂C = 0: μ' is finite on compacts, ξ' is strongly measurable, |ξ'(x)(α)| = 0 ≤ |α|, and ∂C(η) = 0 = ∫ξ'(η)dμ' for every test form η.

2. Apply the ISP hypothesis of C to the representations (μ, ξ) of C and (μ', ξ') of ∂C, to f and to L = 1: for L¹-a.e. t, for all currents A ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(ℝ^P) and B ∈ 𝒟_d(ℝ^P) with A(ω) = ∫_{f<t} ξ(ω)dμ and B(η) = ∫_{f<t} ξ'(η)dμ' for all test forms, ∂A − B is integer multiplicity. Let N be the set of t ∈ ℝ at which this property fails; by ae_iff, N is Lebesgue-null.

3. Apply (SL) with k := d, U := ℝ^P (open), T := C, the representations (μ, ξ) and (μ', ξ'), f and L := 1; all its hypotheses hold (finiteness on compacts, measurability, the pointwise bounds, the representations of C and of ∂C from step 1, f Lipschitz). This gives currents A_t ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(ℝ^P), B_t ∈ 𝒟_d(ℝ^P), t ∈ ℝ, with A_t(ω) = ∫_{f<t} ξ(ω)dμ, B_t(η) = ∫_{f<t} ξ'(η)dμ' = 0 (an integral against the zero measure), ∂A_t(η) = B_t(η) whenever tsupport η ∩ {f = t} = ∅, and M_W(∂A_t − B_t) ≤ 1·liminf_{h↓0} h⁻¹μ(W ∩ {t − h < f < t}) for every open W.

4. Fix ρ > 0 with ρ ∉ N and put A := A_ρ. Then A(ω) = ∫_{B_ρ(x₁)} ξ(ω)dμ for every test form ω. All values of B_ρ vanish, so B_ρ = 0 and ∂A − B_ρ = ∂A (extensionality of currents).

5. (Integer multiplicity.) Since ρ ∉ N, the property of step 2 holds at t = ρ; applied to A_ρ and B_ρ, whose values are given by the formulas of step 3, it shows that ∂A − B_ρ = ∂A is integer multiplicity.

6. (Support.) Let y ∈ ℝ^P with y ∉ ∂B_ρ(x₁), let r := |dist(y, x₁) − ρ|/2 > 0 and W' := B_r(y), an open set whose closure B̄_r(y) is compact. For z ∈ W', |dist(z, x₁) − dist(y, x₁)| ≤ |z − y| < r < |dist(y, x₁) − ρ|, so dist(z, x₁) ≠ ρ; hence every test form η with tsupport η ⊆ W' satisfies tsupport η ∩ {f = ρ} = ∅ and therefore ∂A(η) = B_ρ(η) = 0 by step 3. Thus ∂A vanishes on W', so W' is contained in the zero region of ∂A and y ∉ spt ∂A. Hence spt ∂A ⊆ ∂B_ρ(x₁).

7. (Mass.) Step 3 with the open set W := ℝ^P gives M(∂A) = M_{ℝ^P}(∂A − B_ρ) ≤ 1·liminf_{h↓0} h⁻¹μ(ℝ^P ∩ {ρ − h < f < ρ}) = liminf_{h↓0} h⁻¹μ({x : ρ − h < |x − x₁| < ρ}) (the factor (1 : ℝ≥0) cast to [0, ∞] is 1, and ℝ^P ∩ X = X). ∎
proof_key_steps: Slice by the 1-Lipschitz f = |· − x₁|, representing ∂C = 0 by the zero measure and zero field.
ISP yields a Lebesgue-null set N outside of which ∂A_t − B_t is integer multiplicity.
(SL) gives A_t = C⌞{f < t}, B_t = 0, the vanishing of ∂A_t off {f = t} and the liminf mass bound.
For ρ ∉ N: ∂A_ρ is integer multiplicity, spt ∂A_ρ ⊆ ∂B_ρ(x₁), and M(∂A_ρ) ≤ liminf_h h⁻¹μ{ρ − h < |x − x₁| < ρ}.

Source: Steps 3–6 of the supplied proof (Simon Ch. 6, 8.2 (2)–(4) with the parent's corrections: the lower density replaces Θ^{*n}, and the support of the filling is controlled through the isoperimetric/deformation bound), with the same constants. Children used: slice (Step 4), radius (Steps 3, 5) and mass_gap (Step 6, n = 1).

Notation: n := d + 1, ω_n := unitBallVolume n = L^n(B_1(0)) and w := ω_n read as a real number; for ρ ∈ ℝ, F(ρ) := μ(B_ρ(x₁)) read as a real number; M(·) = mass on ℝ^P read as a real number when finite.

0. (ω_n.) 0 < ω_n < ∞: the unit ball of ℝ^n is bounded, so it has finite Lebesgue measure, and it is a nonempty open set, so its measure is positive. Hence w > 0 and ω_n = w (as an element of [0, ∞]).

1. (Constants; they depend only on P and d.) If d = 0 (n = 1) put η₀ := 1/(4w). If d = m + 1 (n = m + 2 ≥ 2), let c ≥ 1 be the constant given by (ISO) for (P, m), put K₀ := c·(2c)^{1/(m+1)}·(2n)^{n/(m+1)} > 0 and η₀ := min{(2K₀)^{−(m+1)}/w, 1/(4cnw)} > 0; then (i) K₀·(η₀w)^{1/(m+1)} ≤ 1/2 (because η₀w ≤ (2K₀)^{−(m+1)}) and (ii) 4cnη₀w ≤ 1. In both cases put a := (η₀w)^{1/n} > 0, so that a^n = η₀w (for n = 1, a = η₀w = 1/4). η₀ and a are fixed here, before C, μ, ξ, x₁ and δ are chosen.

2. (A small scale.) Fix C, μ, ξ satisfying the hypotheses, x₁ with liminf_{r↓0} μ(B_r(x₁))/(ω_n r^n) < η₀, and δ > 0. By the definition of liminf, μ(B_r(x₁))/(ω_n r^n) < η₀ holds for r in a set that is frequent along r ↓ 0 (frequently_lt_of_liminf_lt), while 0 < r < δ holds eventually; choose s ∈ (0, δ) with μ(B_s(x₁))/(ω_n s^n) < η₀. Since ω_n s^n ∈ (0, ∞), μ(B_s(x₁)) < η₀·ω_n·s^n = η₀w s^n = (as)^n (ENNReal.div_lt_iff).

3. (Good radius and slice.) The child slice (with (SL), ∂C = 0, the representation (μ, ξ) and ISP) applied at x₁ gives a Lebesgue-null set N ⊆ ℝ. The child radius (with n ≥ 1, a > 0, s > 0, μ(B_s(x₁)) < (as)^n and N) gives ρ ∈ (0, s), ρ ∉ N, with μ(∂B_ρ(x₁)) = 0 and ℓ := liminf_{h↓0} h⁻¹μ({ρ − h < |x − x₁| < ρ}) ≤ b, where b := 2na·F(ρ)^{(n−1)/n} ≥ 0. Applying slice at ρ (ρ > 0, ρ ∉ N) gives A ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with A(ω) = ∫_{B_ρ(x₁)} ξ(ω)dμ for all test forms ω, such that Z := ∂A ∈ 𝒟_d(ℝ^P) is integer multiplicity, spt Z ⊆ ∂B_ρ(x₁), and M(Z) ≤ ℓ ≤ b. In particular M(Z) < ∞ and M := M(Z) ≤ b. Moreover F(ρ) ≤ F(s) < (as)^n.

4. (Case n = 1, d = 0.) Here b = 2a·F(ρ)^0 = 2a = 1/2 < 1, so Z is an integer multiplicity 0-current with M(Z) < 1, and the child mass_gap (with (MR)) gives Z = 0. Take S := 0 ∈ 𝒟_1(ℝ^P). Then ∂S = 0 = Z = ∂A; M(S) = 0 ≤ ½·μ(B_ρ(x₁)) (every value of S is 0); and spt S = ∅ ⊆ B̄_{(1+3√P)δ}(x₁), since the zero current vanishes on every ball B_1(y), an open set with compact closure, so every y lies in its zero region.

5. (Case n = m + 2 ≥ 2.) Z ∈ 𝒟_{m+1}(ℝ^P) satisfies ∂Z = ∂∂A = 0 (GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_boundary), is integer multiplicity, has M(Z) < ∞, and spt Z is compact: it is closed (the complement of the open zero region) and contained in the compact sphere ∂B_ρ(x₁). By (ISO) for (P, m) there is an integer multiplicity Y ∈ 𝒟_{m+2}(ℝ^P) = 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with ∂Y = Z, M(Y) ≤ c(2cM)^{1/(m+1)}M and spt Y ⊆ thickening(3√P(2cM)^{1/(m+1)}, spt Z). Take S := Y, so ∂S = Z = ∂A.
(a) Mass. Since 0 ≤ M ≤ b and n/(m+1) > 0: c(2cM)^{1/(m+1)}M = c(2c)^{1/(m+1)}M^{1/(m+1)}M^1 = c(2c)^{1/(m+1)}M^{1/(m+1)+1} = c(2c)^{1/(m+1)}M^{n/(m+1)} (Real.mul_rpow for the nonnegative factors 2c and M, and Real.rpow_add', which needs only M ≥ 0 and 1/(m+1) + 1 ≠ 0, so it also covers M = 0) ≤ c(2c)^{1/(m+1)}b^{n/(m+1)} (Real.rpow_le_rpow), and b^{n/(m+1)} = (2n)^{n/(m+1)}·a^{n/(m+1)}·(F(ρ)^{(m+1)/n})^{n/(m+1)} = (2n)^{n/(m+1)}(η₀w)^{1/(m+1)}F(ρ) (a^{n/(m+1)} = ((η₀w)^{1/n})^{n/(m+1)} = (η₀w)^{1/(m+1)}). Hence c(2cM)^{1/(m+1)}M ≤ K₀(η₀w)^{1/(m+1)}F(ρ) ≤ F(ρ)/2 by (i), and M(S) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(F(ρ)/2) = ½·μ(B_ρ(x₁)).
(b) Support. Since F(ρ) < (as)^n and u ↦ u^{(m+1)/n} is monotone on [0, ∞), b = 2na·F(ρ)^{(m+1)/n} ≤ 2na(as)^{m+1} = 2n·a^n·s^{m+1} = 2nη₀w·s^{m+1}. Hence 2cM ≤ 4cnη₀w·s^{m+1} ≤ s^{m+1} by (ii), so (2cM)^{1/(m+1)} ≤ s. If y ∈ spt S, there is z ∈ spt Z ⊆ ∂B_ρ(x₁) with |y − z| < 3√P(2cM)^{1/(m+1)} ≤ 3√P·s (Metric.mem_thickening_iff), so |y − x₁| < ρ + 3√P·s ≤ (1 + 3√P)δ because ρ < s < δ. Thus spt S ⊆ B̄_{(1+3√P)δ}(x₁).

6. (Conclusion.) In both cases 0 < ρ < s < δ, μ(∂B_ρ(x₁)) = 0, A(ω) = ∫_{B_ρ(x₁)} ξ(ω)dμ for all ω, ∂S = ∂A, M(S) ≤ ½·μ(B_ρ(x₁)) and spt S ⊆ B̄_{(1+3√P)δ}(x₁). ∎

subproblems.title: Points with small fillings at all scales form a μ-null set (Simon 8.2 (4)–(6), corrected)
subproblems.statement: Assume (VO), the exact frozen statement of dtc_vanish_off_support, which appears verbatim as the first hypothesis of the Lean statement (a current vanishes on test forms whose topological support is disjoint from its support). Let P, d ∈ ℕ, C ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(ℝ^P), μ a Borel measure on ℝ^P with μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K and μ(W) = M_W(C) for every open W, ξ a μ-a.e. strongly measurable field of (d+1)-vectors with |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for μ-a.e. x and all α, with C(ω) = ∫ξ(ω)dμ for every test form ω. Let κ, λ ∈ ℝ (κ and lam in Lean) with 0 ≤ κ < 1 ≤ λ, and let E ⊆ ℝ^P be any set such that for every x ∈ E and every δ > 0 there are ρ ∈ (0, δ) with μ(∂B_ρ(x)) = 0 and currents A, S ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(ℝ^P) with A(ω) = ∫_{B_ρ(x)} ξ(ω) dμ for every test form ω, ∂S = ∂A, M(S) ≤ κ·μ(B_ρ(x)) and spt S ⊆ B̄_{λδ}(x). Then μ(E) = 0.

Source: Steps 7–10 of the supplied proof (Simon Ch. 6, 8.2 (4)–(6): disjoint balls, comparison currents X_i = S_i − C⌞B_i, the cone inequality and lower semicontinuity of M_W), carried out for each admissible test form separately: for a W-admissible ω, C(ω) is bounded by μ(W ∖ ⋃B_i) + ΣM(S_i) + Σ|X_i(ω)|, which is exactly the estimate behind M_W(C_δ) ≤ μ(W ∖ ⋃B_i) + κΣμ(B_i) and C_δ ⇀ C in Steps 8–9; taking the supremum over ω replaces lower semicontinuity. Steps 1–2 of the supplied proof (Borel measurability of the density, inner regularity) are not needed because E is an arbitrary set. Children used: cone and covering. (λ denotes the Lean variable lam.)

Notation: n := d + 1; |·| is the Euclidean coefficient norm of covectors; a test form ω ∈ 𝒟^n(ℝ^P) is G-admissible if tsupport ω ⊆ G and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x, and M_G(T) = sup{max(T(ω), 0) : ω G-admissible} (GeometricCurrentOn.massOn); M := M_{ℝ^P}; masses and measures are read as real numbers when finite.

1. (Elementary facts.) For S, A ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P):
(a) (S − A)(ω) = S(ω) − A(ω), and ∂(S − A) = ∂S − ∂A, since ∂(S − A)(η) = (S − A)(dη) = S(dη) − A(dη) (extensionality of currents).
(b) If M(T) < ∞ and ω is ℝ^P-admissible, then |T(ω)| ≤ M(T): T(ω) ≤ M(T) by the definition of M (GeometricCurrentOn.le_massOn), and −T(ω) = T(−ω) ≤ M(T) because −ω is admissible (|−β| = |β|).
(c) M(S − A) ≤ M(S) + M(A): for an ℝ^P-admissible ω, (S − A)(ω) = S(ω) + A(−ω) and max(S(ω) + A(−ω), 0) ≤ max(S(ω), 0) + max(A(−ω), 0) ≤ M(S) + M(A); take the supremum over ω.
(d) spt(S − A) ⊆ spt S ∪ spt A: if y ∉ spt S ∪ spt A, there are open sets W₁, W₂ ∋ y with compact closures such that S vanishes on every test form supported in W₁ and A on every test form supported in W₂; then W₁ ∩ W₂ is an open neighbourhood of y with compact closure on which S − A vanishes, so y lies in the zero region of S − A.
(e) If A(ω) = ∫_{B_ρ(x)} ξ(ω)dμ for all ω, then M(A) ≤ μ(B_ρ(x)) and spt A ⊆ B̄_ρ(x). For ℝ^P-admissible ω, |ξ(y)(ω(y))| ≤ |ω(y)| ≤ 1 for μ-a.e. y, so A(ω) ≤ μ(B_ρ(x)) (finite: B̄_ρ(x) is compact); take the supremum. If y ∉ B̄_ρ(x), put r := (|y − x| − ρ)/2 > 0; the ball W' := B_r(y) is open with compact closure and disjoint from B_ρ(x), so every test form ω with tsupport ω ⊆ W' vanishes on B_ρ(x) and A(ω) = ∫_{B_ρ(x)} ξ(y)(0) dμ = 0; hence y ∉ spt A.

2. (Reduction to bounded pieces.) E = ⋃_{k∈ℕ} E_k with E_k := E ∩ B_k(0), so by countable subadditivity (measure_iUnion_null) it suffices to show μ(E_k) = 0 for every k; each E_k satisfies the hypothesis of the statement because E_k ⊆ E. Fix k and put E' := E_k and W := B_{k+1}(0): W is open, E' ⊆ W, and μ(W) ≤ μ(B̄_{k+1}(0)) < ∞.

3. (Estimate for one admissible form.) Claim: every W-admissible ω satisfies C(ω) ≤ μ(W) − (1 − κ)·μ(E').
Let g(y) := ξ(y)(ω(y)). g is μ-a.e. strongly measurable (ContinuousLinearMap.aestronglyMeasurable_comp₂ applied to the identity map of Λ_{d+1}(ℝ^P) = (Λ^{d+1}(ℝ^P) →L ℝ), with ξ μ-a.e. strongly measurable and ω continuous) and |g(y)| ≤ |ω(y)| ≤ 1 for μ-a.e. y. Since ω = 0 outside W, g = 0 outside W, so C(ω) = ∫ g dμ = ∫_W g dμ. Let c ≥ 0 be the constant given by the child cone (with (VO)) for the test form ω of degree d + 1. Fix ε ∈ (0, 1 − κ] and put δ₀ := ε/((c + 1)·λ·(1 + κ)) > 0.
(i) For every x ∈ E' and δ' > 0 there is ρ ∈ (0, δ') with ∫_{B̄_ρ(x)} g dμ ≤ (κ + ε)·μ(B̄_ρ(x)). Indeed, apply the hypothesis at x with δ := min(δ', δ₀) > 0: it gives ρ ∈ (0, δ), μ(∂B_ρ(x)) = 0 and A, S as in the statement. Put X := S − A. By 1(a), ∂X = ∂S − ∂A = 0. By 1(c), 1(e) and the hypothesis, M(X) ≤ M(S) + M(A) ≤ κμ(B_ρ(x)) + μ(B_ρ(x)) = (1 + κ)μ(B_ρ(x)) < ∞. By 1(d), 1(e) and the hypothesis, spt X ⊆ B̄_{λδ}(x) ∪ B̄_ρ(x) = B̄_{λδ}(x), since ρ < δ ≤ λδ. The child cone with x₀ := x and ϱ := λδ > 0 gives |X(ω)| ≤ c·λδ·M(X) ≤ cλδ(1 + κ)μ(B_ρ(x)) ≤ ε·μ(B_ρ(x)), because cλδ(1 + κ) ≤ cλδ₀(1 + κ) = cε/(c + 1) ≤ ε. Since ω is also ℝ^P-admissible and M(S) ≤ κμ(B_ρ(x)) < ∞, 1(b) gives S(ω) ≤ κμ(B_ρ(x)). Hence ∫_{B_ρ(x)} g dμ = A(ω) = S(ω) − X(ω) ≤ (κ + ε)μ(B_ρ(x)). Finally B̄_ρ(x) ∖ B_ρ(x) = ∂B_ρ(x) is μ-null, so ∫_{B̄_ρ(x)} g dμ = ∫_{B_ρ(x)} g dμ and μ(B̄_ρ(x)) = μ(B_ρ(x)).
(ii) The child covering, applied with μ, g, θ := κ + ε ≤ 1, the set E' and the open set W ⊇ E' with μ(W) < ∞, using (i), gives ∫_W g dμ ≤ μ(W) − (1 − κ − ε)·μ(E').
(iii) Hence C(ω) ≤ μ(W) − (1 − κ − ε)·μ(E') for every ε ∈ (0, 1 − κ]; letting ε ↓ 0 proves the claim.

4. (Conclusion.) Put β := μ(W) − (1 − κ)·μ(E') ∈ ℝ. By step 3, max(C(ω), 0) ≤ max(β, 0) for every W-admissible ω, so by the hypothesis on μ and the definition of M_W as a supremum, μ(W) = M_W(C) ≤ max(β, 0) (ENNReal.ofReal β). If μ(E') > 0, then μ(W) ≥ μ(E') > 0 and β < μ(W) because 1 − κ > 0, so max(β, 0) < μ(W), a contradiction. Hence μ(E') = 0, i.e. μ(E_k) = 0 for every k, and μ(E) = 0 by step 2. ∎
proof_key_steps: Current calculus for X = S − A: ∂X = ∂S − ∂A = 0, M(X) ≤ M(S) + M(A) ≤ (1 + κ)μ(B_ρ(x)), spt X ⊆ spt S ∪ spt A ⊆ B̄_{λδ}(x).
Reduce to E ∩ B_k(0) and the open set W = B_{k+1}(0) of finite measure.
For a W-admissible ω, cone gives |X(ω)| ≤ εμ(B_ρ(x)) at scales δ ≤ δ₀(ω, ε), so ∫_{B̄_ρ(x)} ξ(ω)dμ = A(ω) = S(ω) − X(ω) ≤ (κ + ε)μ(B̄_ρ(x)).
covering gives C(ω) = ∫_W ξ(ω)dμ ≤ μ(W) − (1 − κ − ε)μ(E'); let ε ↓ 0.
Supremum over ω: μ(W) = M_W(C) ≤ μ(W) − (1 − κ)μ(E'), hence μ(E') = 0 and μ(E) = 0.
